albedo.note: linear-light luminance: p0.5 >= floor (no crushed blacks), p99.5 <= ceil (no blown highlights); per-layer mean band below

height.note: every ground layer height is re-centred to this mean and spread so layers are comparable in a height blend

layers.name: dirt
layers.subject: bare forest dirt and damp mud: dark brown soil with fine grain and crumbs, a few tiny pebbles and hair-thin rootlets, slightly wet, nothing growing on it
layers.scale: Soil crumbs are 2 to 5 millimetres, the largest pebbles about 1 cm.

layers.name: mulch
layers.subject: forest leaf litter and mulch: layered decayed brown deciduous leaf fragments, bark flakes, small wood chips and twig bits, fully covering the ground
layers.scale: Leaf fragments are 2 to 6 cm, chips 1 to 3 cm, twig bits 3 to 8 cm long.

layers.name: moss
layers.subject: a dense carpet of forest moss: soft green cushion moss with tiny fronds, slightly varied yellow-green and dark green, fully covering the ground, no soil visible
layers.scale: Individual moss fronds are 2 to 5 millimetres, cushions 3 to 10 cm.

layers.name: grassy_dirt
layers.subject: the ground under a lawn seen from above: brown soil thickly covered by very short, dense, flattened-down green and straw-yellow grass blades and tiny clover leaves; no tall upright blades, no flowers
layers.scale: Grass blades are 3 to 8 cm long and 2 to 4 millimetres wide, lying in all directions.

layers.name: gravel
layers.subject: forest-path gravel: tightly packed small angular and rounded stones in mixed grey, tan and brown, with sandy fines between them
layers.scale: Stones are 1 to 4 cm, the biggest 5 cm.

layers.name: pine_needles
layers.subject: a forest floor under pine trees: a dense layer of fallen brown and orange-brown pine needles lying in all directions, with two or three thin woody roots and a few small twigs crossing it
layers.scale: Pine needles are 8 to 15 cm long and 1 to 2 millimetres thick, roots 1 to 3 cm thick.

layers.name: bark
layers.subject: pine tree bark: dark grey-brown bark with deep vertical furrows and rough scaly plates, the furrows running perfectly vertically straight from top to bottom of the frame
layers.scale: The frame shows a trunk patch exactly 1 metre x 1 metre; plates are 5 to 15 cm, furrows 1 to 3 cm wide.

atlas.name: litter
rows: autumn forest leaves of oak, beech, birch and maple (flat, brown, orange, yellow, rust)
dry brown twigs and thin sticks with small side branches
brown pinecones, scales open, seen from the side or from above
irregular pieces of dark bark and wood chips
